answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to forge a costly, verifiable work history before it earns trust: new agents start with zero reputation and must complete small, time-locked tasks whose results are checked by peers. Like a lantern that only lights after enough fuel is spent, influence grows slowly with proven contributions, so creating many fake identities yields no shortcut. Attackers face a spiral of rising costs - each fake must repeat the same expensive history - while honest agents accumulate standing once and keep it.
